segments.text: A smoke alarm can be wrong in two ways.
segments.caption: A smoke alarm can be wrong in two ways.

segments.text: It rings when there's no fire, or it stays silent during a real one.
segments.caption: It rings when there's no fire, or it stays silent during a real one.

segments.text: Statistical tests make the same two mistakes.
segments.caption: Statistical tests make the same two mistakes.

segments.text: Here's the definition, in simple words.
segments.caption: Here's the definition, in simple words.

segments.text: A Type one error is a false alarm: rejecting the null when it was actually true.
segments.caption: A Type 1 error is a false alarm: rejecting the null when it was actually true.

segments.text: A Type two error is a miss: keeping the null when it was actually false.
segments.caption: A Type 2 error is a miss: keeping the null when it was actually false.

segments.text: Picture all four outcomes.
segments.caption: Picture all four outcomes.

segments.text: The null is either true or false, and you either reject it or keep it.
segments.caption: The null is either true or false, and you either reject it or keep it.

segments.text: Two boxes are correct. The other two are the errors.
segments.caption: Two boxes are correct. The other two are the errors.

segments.text: Think of a medical test.
segments.caption: Think of a medical test.

segments.text: Telling a healthy person they're sick? Type one: a false alarm.
segments.caption: Telling a healthy person they're sick? Type 1: a false alarm.

segments.text: Telling a sick person they're healthy? Type two: a miss.
segments.caption: Telling a sick person they're healthy? Type 2: a miss.

segments.text: The chance of a Type one error is called alpha, usually five percent.
segments.caption: The chance of a Type 1 error is called alpha, usually 5%.

segments.text: So when nothing's going on, about one test in twenty still raises a false alarm.
segments.caption: So when nothing's going on, about 1 test in 20 still raises a false alarm.

segments.text: The chance of a Type two error is beta, and one minus beta is called power.
segments.caption: The chance of a Type 2 error is beta, and 1 minus beta is called power.

segments.text: Here's the catch: the two errors trade off.
segments.caption: Here's the catch: the two errors trade off.

segments.text: Make the test stricter, and you get fewer false alarms, but more misses.
segments.caption: Make the test stricter, and you get fewer false alarms, but more misses.

segments.text: The way to reduce both? Collect more data.
segments.caption: The way to reduce both? Collect more data.

segments.text: So which mistake is worse? It depends.
segments.caption: So which mistake is worse? It depends.

segments.text: Missing a disease can be deadly, so screening tests avoid Type two errors.
segments.caption: Missing a disease can be deadly, so screening tests avoid Type 2 errors.

segments.text: Jailing an innocent person is a Type one error, so courts demand strong evidence.
segments.caption: Jailing an innocent person is a Type 1 error, so courts demand strong evidence.

segments.text: So remember: Type one is a false alarm. Type two is a miss.
segments.caption: So remember: Type 1 is a false alarm. Type 2 is a miss.

segments.text: Stricter tests trade one for the other, and more data helps with both.
segments.caption: Stricter tests trade one for the other, and more data helps with both.

segments.caption: Which type of error is that?

segments.text: Type one!
segments.caption: Type 1!

segments.text: The null says the email is normal, and the filter wrongly rejected it. A false alarm.
